raw_response:
I am 70 years old this year. I never went to school, not one day. My father taught me to farm, and I have done it for 50 years. I have 6.8 mu in Quzhou, just me and my old woman. We grow wheat in winter, maize in summer on 4.8 mu, and I keep 2 mu for cotton because the price was okay last year and I need the cash.

For the wheat: it is already in the ground. Last fall I rotary tilled and sowed the improved seed I saved from the year before — about 25 jin per mu. I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as base. Now in spring I will irrigate three times from my well: when it turns green, when it shoots up, and when the grain is filling. Each time I flood the furrows. I top-dress with urea twice: 40 jin per mu at green-up, another 40 jin at jointing. That is about 25 kg of nitrogen per mu in total. Some people say it is too much, but last year I put less and my wheat looked yellow next to Lao Wang's field. Better to waste fertilizer than lose grain. I spray once for aphids if I see them. I expect 860 jin per mu, about 430 kg.

For the maize: after I cut the wheat in June, I plant hybrid maize seed on the same 4.8 mu. I buy the seed from the dealer in town, 3 jin per mu. I do not till the ground — there is no time, and the neighbors sow directly into the wheat stubble. I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu in the rows at sowing. When the plants are knee-high, I put 60 jin of urea per mu. That is about 20 kg of nitrogen. I irrigate twice: once at the big trumpet stage, once when the tassels come out, if the rain does not come. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once. I expect 1000 jin per mu, about 500 kg.

For the cotton: I plough the 2 mu deep because cotton needs loose soil. I plant the improved cotton seed in April, the same kind I have used for years. I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, and 40 jin of urea per mu when it flowers. That is about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu. I irrigate three times: at flowering, at boll-setting, and in August. I spray three times for the bollworm — that worm eats everything if you let it. Picking cotton is hard for my old hands, but seed cotton sells for good money. I expect 440 jin per mu, about 220 kg.

I do not try new things. The dealer talks about new fertilizer, new seed, but I do not listen unless I see Lao Wang or Old Zhang use it first and their field looks better than mine. Fertilizer costs money, but a bad harvest costs everything. I would rather put one more bag than one less. My well pump costs electricity, but without water in Hebei, nothing grows.
